recent_posts.title: Automatic App Store Uploads w/ Bitrise and CI/CD
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of setting up CI/CD for iOS development using Bitrise, covering two automation workflows: a run-tests workflow triggered on every branch push (running unit and UI tests in parallel on a fresh Mac Mini environment), and an archive-and-export workflow triggered on merges to main that handles code signing and automatically uploads builds to App Store Connect/TestFlight. The demo uses a habit tracker app with a new streaks feature to show the full pipeline end-to-end, from committing code to seeing a new TestFlight build appear on a physical device without any manual steps.

recent_posts.title: iOS Agent Skills, App Store Connect CLI, Foundation Models Tokens & More
recent_posts.summary: A Swift News roundup covering several iOS development topics: the App Store Connect CLI tool that enables terminal-based automation of App Store tasks (TestFlight, metadata localization, PPP pricing) and its integration with AI agent skills via Codex/Claude Code; Paul Hudson's SwiftUI, Swift Concurrency, Swift Data, and Swift Testing agent skills that steer LLMs toward modern best practices; a Swift Concurrency learning roadmap from beginner to advanced; token usage tracking in Apple's on-device Foundation Models (iOS 26.4, 4096-token context window); and reflections on context switching challenges when using AI agents across multiple projects simultaneously.

recent_posts.title: Xcode Agentic Coding, AI Anxiety, iOS 26 Adoption, Micro-Interactions
recent_posts.summary: Xcode 26.3 RC introduces agentic coding with OpenAI and Anthropic integration, allowing AI agents to build projects, validate UI, and access Apple documentation directly in the IDE. iOS 26 has reached 66.53% adoption despite divisive design changes. The article addresses developer anxiety about AI's impact on the profession, arguing that while AI lowers barriers to basic coding, craft and quality remain differentiators—especially in Apple's ecosystem where micro-interactions and design philosophy matter. Includes promotion for Eraser, a menu bar tool for managing Xcode storage.

recent_posts.title: How to implement concentric corners in SwiftUI for iOS 26
recent_posts.summary: iOS 26 introduces concentricity as a core design principle where rounded corners of nested views align perfectly. SwiftUI provides the concentric rectangle API to automatically calculate corner radii based on proximity to container edges. The containerShape modifier sets the baseline for subviews, while the isUniform parameter ensures all corners match. The technique works with images via clipShape, buttons, and full-screen sheets, creating visual harmony between UI elements and device hardware.

recent_posts.title: Bleeding Edge AI Work, What's New in Swift, Concurrency, Apple Ads
recent_posts.summary: A roundup covering bleeding-edge AI development workflows (featuring a top-10 Codex user's approach to building software with minimal code reading), the official Swift blog's monthly update series, two complementary Swift concurrency resources (a beginner-friendly overview and an in-depth migration guide), and Apple's 2026 expansion of App Store search ad slots beyond the top position.

recent_posts.title: Creating App Store screenshots with AppScreens
recent_posts.summary: AppScreens is a tool that simplifies creating App Store screenshots for iOS apps. It offers pre-designed templates that can be customized, automatically generates text based on app descriptions, handles multiple device sizes (iPhone 6.9" and iPad 13" cover all variants), supports localization, and uploads directly to App Store Connect. The workflow involves taking simulator screenshots in Xcode, uploading them to AppScreens, selecting and customizing a template, and pushing everything to App Store Connect with one click instead of manually managing different sizes and formats.

Indie development challenges are explored, including isolation, decision paralysis, and work-life balance struggles. A developer shares 100 lessons from bootstrapping an app to a seven-figure exit, covering onboarding, user support, and review management strategies.

recent_posts.title: Swift SDK for Android, Shipaton Winners, Foundation Models, Scroll Performance & More.
recent_posts.summary: Swift SDK for Android reaches nightly preview release, enabling shared business logic between iOS and Android apps through Swift-to-Java interoperability. The post covers SwiftUI scroll performance optimization techniques for achieving 120fps, including comparisons between VStack, LazyVStack, and List implementations. Additional topics include Apple's Foundation Models code-along Q&A, text concatenation deprecation in iOS 26 favoring interpolation for better localization, iPhone 17 screen specifications, and Revenue Cat's Ship-a-ton 2025 hackathon winners.

recent_posts.title: Indie Dev Tip - Lifestyle Fit #iosdev #indiedev #iosdeveloper
recent_posts.summary: Advice for independent developers on choosing project scope based on personal circumstances. Developers with limited time (family, full-time job) should focus on simple, completable apps they can polish and market. Those with more availability can pursue larger projects or experiment with multiple small apps. The key is honestly assessing available time and selecting project complexity accordingly.

recent_posts.title: Indie Dev Tip - Minimize Complexity.
recent_posts.summary: Keep indie app projects small and focused on solving one problem well. Build apps with finite scope that can be completed, like an AI roast generator or F1 stats widgets. This approach enables making multiple small bets to test what resonates with users, rather than investing years into a single complex app with endless features that may never feel finished.
